item.title: Swedish word of the day: lussekatt
item.description: Will you have a lussekatt this weekend? Or two?

item.title: Moderate youth chair calls for Sweden to adjust 'track change' law
item.description: The Moderate Party's youth wing has called for a law removing the right of asylum seekers to "change track" and instead apply for a work permit to be changed so that more who have managed to get stable jobs are allowed to stay in Sweden.

item.title: GOATWATCH: Here's how you can livestream Sweden's Christmas goat
item.description: The Christmas Goat in the Swedish city of Gävle has become a worldwide symbol of the season for many who eagerly follow news of the straw goat to see if it survives until Christmas day. Here's where you can watch it online.

item.title: Tax cuts, longer citizenship wait and an election: What changes in Sweden in 2026
item.description: Sweden's government is bringing in far-reaching tax cuts, lower daycare fees, an increase in the wait for citizenship to 8 years, and on top of all that, there's a general election. Here's what's happening in Sweden in 2026.

item.title: Saints, spooks, and eyeballs: An immigrant's view of Lucia in Sweden
item.description: It's mid-December and in Sweden that means Lucia: groups of white-robed people singing with candles on their heads. But what exactly is this strangely beautiful (and beautifully eerie) celebration about, and where did it come from?

item.title: How can Sweden get better at integrating immigrants?
item.description: In this week's podcast: How Sweden can get beyond immigrant stereotypes, Indians' relationship with Sweden, Sweden reacts to US talk of 'civilisational erasure' in Europe, how to get your Swedish to 'gymnasium' level, and Princess Sofia met Jeffrey Epstein.

item.title: Sweden to tighten income requirements for family reunion
item.description: The Swedish government and Sweden Democrats are pushing forward with plans to tighten the requirements for family reunion, by raising the income requirement by 30 percent, among other measures.

item.title: Lessons from a Skåne julbord on how we oversimplify Sweden
item.description: The Local's Nordic Editor Richard Orange rounds up the biggest stories of the week in our Inside Sweden newsletter.

item.title: 'I feel alienated': American dual nationals in Europe ready to renounce citizenship
item.description: Dual-national American readers across Europe say they would give up their US passports to stay European if they were forced to, with many citing political disillusionment, fears for safety, and the feeling of belonging to their adopted country.

item.title: The little-known agreement that sets Europe's citizenship guidelines
item.description: An important but hardly-known international agreement signed by 29 European countries has established common principles for citizenship rules, rights and duties associated to multiple citizenship, explains Claudia Delpero.
